name: Mi'kmaq

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Mi'kmaq (mikm1235).

notes: Algic (Algonquian) language of Atlantic Canada. The grapheme map reads the Listuguj orthography, which the shipped wikipron gold uses; the Francis-Smith letters k and á é í ó ú are carried as well, but Francis-Smith is not modelled in full here, since its schwa letter ɨ is absent. An apostrophe after a vowel marks vowel length and after a consonant marks schwa: mic_mikmaqonline gives a'pi as aa-bi, gta'n as ek-taan, p'tew as be-dew and put'p as bu-dep; the orthographic apostrophe does not represent a glottal stop. Obstruents p t k q j s are voiceless phonemes realized voiced between sonorants (mic_fidelholtz1968 p. 12), and Listuguj writes /k/ as g, so g and gw read as k and kʷ (mic_mikmaqonline gives alug as a-luk and agumegw as a-gu-mekw); that intervocalic allophony is left unencoded. Acute-marked vowels denote length. The letter q represents a velar/uvular fricative [x]. mic_fidelholtz1968 p. 12 glosses the short mid vowels directly, e as in French après and o as in French comme, i.e. open-mid [ɛ] and [ɔ]; this confirms the shipped open-mid values and is the reason the mid-vowel change to close-mid is refused. Schwa epenthesis in initial and medial clusters (agnutmaqan [akənutəmaxan]) is predictable but unencoded, and raises the PER floor along with predictable stress.
